body:
I checked 5166b72 on Windows x64 (Python 3.12.14, Torch 2.11.0+cpu, Gymnasium 1.3.0) and found a test-fixture portability issue: _vector_env hardcodes context="forkserver", which Windows does not provide. The four-file command from your description reports 17 failed, 31 passed; all 17 async cases fail with ValueError: cannot find context for 'forkserver'.

Keeping forkserver where supported and falling back to spawn resolves it:

    from multiprocessing import get_all_start_methods

    context = "forkserver" if "forkserver" in get_all_start_methods() else "spawn"
    kwargs = {"context": context} if vector == "async" else {}

With only that fixture change, the same command reports 48 passed, no skips (176.89 seconds). Ruff check/format and diff checks pass. This preserves real async workers and all assertions, and provides Windows validation of your terminal-observation fix without changing production code.

This used your scripted policy and software environments, not a learned checkpoint or physical robot. I did not run the full suite or independently repeat the main-vs-PR evaluator comparison.

AI disclosure: this portability correction, test execution and review were prepared with substantial assistance from OpenAI Codex.
